For Q4M treatment, the phase III CUATRO registrational study is on track with an expected launch in 2028. For Q4M PrEP, the phase IIb registrational EXTEND study data is progressing with data expected in H2 2026 and launch in H1 2027.

Respiratory.text: Results from the non-registrational, phase IIIb switch trial, NIMBLE, were published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine. The study evaluated patients with severe asthma, already stable on mepolizumab or benralizumab for at least 12 months, who were randomised to continue their biologic or switch to depemokimab. While depemokimab did not show statistical non-inferiority, most patients maintained disease control. Exacerbation rates were low and symptom control/lung function were maintained in all groups suggesting that most participants with severe asthma on mepolizumab or benralizumab may safely switch to twice-yearly depemokimab.

Oncology.text: Jemperli remains the foundation of GSK’s immuno-oncology-based research and development programme. It is the only approved immuno-oncology-based plus carboplatin-paclitaxel (CP) treatment regimen to demonstrate a statistically significant and clinically meaningful overall survival benefit vs. CP alone for the first-line treatment of adult patients with primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer irrespective of biomarker status. Ongoing pivotal trials include those in the AZUR programme (colon / rectal cancers), JADE (head and neck cancer), and DOMENICA (supported-collaborative study with ARCAGY-GINECO in endometrial cancer).

HIV.heading: HIV
HIV.text:
As a pioneer in long-acting injectables, ViiV Healthcare, majority owned by GSK, remains focused on advancing the next-generation of INSTI-powered HIV innovation.

In Q3, topline phase IIIb CROWN data demonstrated Cabenuva ’s (cabotegravir + rilpivirine; CAB + RPV LA) superior efficacy versus standard of care oral anti-retroviral therapy in people with unsuppressed HIV. These data address an important unmet need and significant growth opportunity and will be shared with health authorities for regulatory review.

At IDWeek 2026, data were shared adding to the significant body of clinical and real-world evidence for long-acting injectables. Five-year OPERA data further reinforced durable effectiveness of CAB LA + RPV in the real world, while prevention data showed very low HIV acquisition with CAB LA for PrEP, consistent with registrational trials. In-vitro data for VH184 – the first potential third-generation INSTI – were also shared further highlighting an enhanced resistance profile against first- and second-generation INSTI-resistant strains.

For the 3x a year long-acting injectable candidate for HIV PrEP (new intramuscular formulation of cabotegravir), data are now in house from the EXTEND 4M pharmacokinetic (PK) study. Analyses are underway to fully characterise the new formulation ahead of sharing the data package with regulators.

Respiratory.text: At the 2026 European Respiratory Society (ERS) Congress, GSK presented data reinforcing depemokimab's differentiated profile, including sustained efficacy over two years in patients with severe asthma and consistent outcomes across key patient subgroups. Results from a patient preference study were also presented showing patient preference for less frequent dosing and identifying dosing frequency as a key reason for non-adherence.

Oncology.text: Core R&D investment increased in Q3 2026 and YTD reflecting progression across the portfolio, primarily in Oncology. This included acceleration in work on ADCs Ris-Rez and Mo-Rez, progress on velzatinib for GIST and, following the Nuvalent acquisition, on Jideytro (zidesamtinib), approved by the FDA in the quarter, and neladalkib. In Specialty Medicines, increased investment was driven by efimosfermin acquired in Q3 2025, depemokimab COPD indication and all indications of felcorekibart (the anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody). Growth was partly offset by lower spend on bepirovirsen which was filed in Q1 2026. Investment also increased on clinical trial programmes associated with mRNA seasonal flu vaccines.
